newsitem.title: UK: Coffee up 40 percent this year, consumers pay.
newsitem.headline: Coffee up 40 percent this year, consumers pay.

text.p: London coffee futures extended a rally on Tuesday to stand some 40 percent higher than a month ago on fears of tight world supply.
Following a lead set in the Netherlands and Germany, coffee roasters in France were the latest to decide to pass on the rise in the price of beans to the consumer in the form of higher retail prices.
A strike called by state workers in Colombia, the number two producer after Brazil, fuelled the latest surge in coffee futures.
The benchmark May contract for Robusta coffee traded on the London Financial Futures Exchange soared $80 at the opening to $1,680 per tonne before profit-taking trimmed gains slightly.
The new advance was inspired by a New York rally in which higher quality Arabica coffee, at 20-month highs, rose to 163 cents/pound.
Colombian union leaders representing 800,000 state workers launched a nationwide strike on Tuesday but its impact on vital economic sectors was not immediately clear.

The strike threw new doubt on coffee supplies beyond concerns about expected low crops in Brazil, traders said. London prices are up about 40 percent since January 7 when the bellwether contract was $1,203 a tonne.
French Cafes Excella SA, a distributor brand, said it planned to raise retail prices by 23 to 24 percent at end February-early March.
Marketing director Jean-Jacques Dothee said this meant a 250 gram-pack would increase by at least two francs or about 35 US cents.
Dothee also said that if the rally in coffee futures continued further hikes in retail prices could not be ruled out in April.
Industry sources said earlier Kraft Jacobs Suchard, part of the Philip Morris group, will also raise French retail prices.
Cocoa prices extended a decline on Tuesday. Traders chiefly blamed a bearish technical outlook as the London May futures price sank 13 pounds sterling to 869 per tonne.
Oil prices, after a long bull run, remained under pressure. But bellwether North Sea Brent crude futures traded in London little changed from Monday at around $20.75 per barrel.
Gold, however, was again weaker just below $340 per ounce in a bullion market that continues haunted by fears of selling from reserves by central banks.
Base metals led by copper and aluminium tended easier in what tradersd said was an expected correction to recent advances, with some profit-taking going on and players adopting short positions.
